title: Magnetic lifting device having pole shoes with spaced apart projections

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.quote: A magnetic device for magnetically coupling to a ferromagnetic body, comprises a housing having a central bore. A plurality of pole sectors arranged within an envelope of the central bore and forming a workpiece contact interface of the magnetic device
features.note: The reference describes a housing containing pole sectors forming a workpiece contact interface and a permanent magnet that is moveable.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.quote: A first permanent magnet. A second permanent being moveable relative to the first permanent magnet. And, an actuator operatively coupled to the at least one second permanent magnet to move the at least one second permanent magnet relative to the
features.note: The reference describes a second permanent magnet that is moveable relative to a first permanent magnet, actuated to move between positions, which implies gripping and release states.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: A plurality of pole sectors arranged within an envelope of the central bore and forming a workpiece contact interface of the magnetic device
features.note: The reference describes pole sectors (pole shoes) arranged within the housing and forming a workpiece contact interface.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: wherein a first sector of the plurality of sectors form a first pole of the magnetic device and a second sector of the plurality of sectors form a second pole of the magnetic device;
features.note: The pole sectors are described as forming poles of the magnetic device, indicating their role in guiding the magnetic field to the workpiece contact surface.
features.refuted: Quote only describes sectors forming poles, not guiding magnetic field to contact surface.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not disclose any specific angles for the workpiece contact surface relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.quote: A magnetic device for magnetically coupling to a ferromagnetic body, comprises a housing having a central bore. A plurality of pole sectors arranged within an envelope of the central bore and forming a workpiece contact interface of the magnetic device
features.note: The reference discloses a magnetic device with a housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes forming a workpiece contact interface, but it does not specify the contact surface angle relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.quote: A magnetic device for magnetically coupling to a ferromagnetic body, comprises a housing having a central bore.
features.note: The reference describes a magnetic device for magnetically coupling to a ferromagnetic body, which implies the magnet in a gripping position would press the workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.refuted: Quote only describes housing with bore, not gripping position or magnetic force pressing workpiece.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.quote: a housing having a vertical axis extending between an upper portion of the housing and a lower portion of the housing; ... the magnetic platter is linearly translatable within the housing along the vertical axis
features.note: The reference discloses a housing with a vertical axis and a magnetic platter linearly translatable along that axis, but it does not explicitly state that the displacement direction is parallel to a longitudinal axis of the housing in a general sense, only a vertical axis.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.quote: each of the plurality of pole sectors comprising a plurality of spaced-apart pole portions arranged at respective distances, wherein a recess of a plurality of recesses separates each pole portion of the plurality of pole portions
features.note: The pole sectors having spaced-apart pole portions and recesses between them constitute an active structure for directing the magnetic field.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference describes recesses and pole portions but does not mention any bevels or bevel angles.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: each of the plurality of pole sectors comprising a plurality of spaced-apart pole portions arranged at respective distances, wherein a recess of a plurality of recesses separates each pole portion of the plurality of pole portions
features.note: The 'spaced-apart pole portions' act as multiple projections that direct the magnetic field and form the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.quote: each of the plurality of pole sectors comprising a plurality of spaced-apart pole portions arranged at respective distances, wherein a recess of a plurality of recesses separates each pole portion of the plurality of pole portions
features.note: The reference discloses adjacent pole portions (projections) with recesses between them, but it does not specify the dimensional relationship between the recess depth/length and the projection length.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any positioning device for the workpiece.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.quote: wherein a first sector of the plurality of sectors form a first pole of the magnetic device and a second sector of the plurality of sectors form a second pole of the magnetic device;
features.note: The reference states that a first sector forms a first pole and a second sector forms a second pole, implying opposite polarities for gripping.
features.refuted: Quote describes sectors forming poles but not magnet position making first north and second south.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.quote: wherein the actuator is one of a hydraulic actuator, a pneumatic actuator, and an electrical actuator.
features.note: The reference explicitly states that the actuator, which moves the magnet, can be hydraulic, pneumatic, or electrical.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not mention any sensors for detecting magnet position or workpiece presence.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.note: The reference does not describe any receptacles for sensors or supply lines.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.quote: wherein the magnetic coupling device is carried by at least one selected from the group of: mechanical gantry, crane hoist, stationary fixture, and a robotic fixture.
features.note: The reference states the magnetic coupling device can be carried by a robotic fixture, which implies a manipulator interface.
features.refuted: Quote describes device carried by various fixtures, not a manipulator interface for attaching.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: The reference does not describe any features for suppressing magnetic field escape or shielding.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.quote: wherein at least one of the plurality of recesses has a depth substantially equal to a thickness of the ferromagnetic body to be coupled to the magnetic device.
features.note: The reference mentions recess depth being substantially equal to workpiece thickness, but not projection length (height) being related to workpiece thickness.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: The reference does not describe any receptacles in the form of a groove.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or bevel angles.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or bevel angles.

claims.quote: A magnetic device for magnetically coupling to a ferromagnetic body, comprises a housing having a central bore.
claims.note: The reference discloses a magnetic device for magnetically coupling to a ferromagnetic body, which is equivalent to a magnetic gripper for gripping a ferromagnetic workpiece, and includes a housing.

claims.quote: A first permanent magnet. A second permanent being moveable relative to the first permanent magnet. And, an actuator operatively coupled to the at least one second permanent magnet to move the at least one second permanent magnet relative to the
claims.note: The reference describes a second permanent magnet being moveable relative to a first permanent magnet, moved by an actuator, which is equivalent to a displaceable magnet between gripping and release positions.

claims.quote: A plurality of pole sectors arranged within an envelope of the central bore and forming a workpiece contact interface of the magnetic device, each of the plurality of pole sectors comprising a plurality of spaced-apart pole portions arranged at respective
claims.note: The reference discloses a plurality of pole sectors forming a workpiece contact interface, which are analogous to pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces designed to guide a magnetic field.
claims.refuted: The quote describes pole sectors within a central bore envelope, not pole shoes attached to the housing as asserted.

claims.note: The reference does not describe a contact surface angle between the workpiece contact surface and the displacement direction, nor does it specify a range for such an angle.
The reference describes pole sectors forming a workpiece contact interface but does not specify a contact surface angle or a range for it.
The reference mentions a housing but does not describe it extending along a longitudinal axis.

claims.quote: a magnetic platter supported by the housing, the magnetic platter comprising more than one permanent magnet portions and a plurality of pole portions, wherein each permanent magnet portion of the one or more permanent magnet portions is arranged adjacent to
claims.note: The reference describes a magnetic platter linearly translatable along a vertical axis, which could be considered a displacement direction. However, it does not explicitly state that this displacement direction is parallel to a longitudinal axis of the housing, as the housing's longitudinal axis is not defined.

claims.quote: a plurality of pole sectors arranged within an envelope of the central bore and forming a workpiece contact interface of the magnetic device, each of the plurality of pole sectors comprising a plurality of spaced-apart pole portions arranged at respective
claims.note: The pole sectors with spaced-apart pole portions act as an active structure for directing the magnetic field to the workpiece contact interface.
claims.refuted: The quote describes pole sectors with pole portions, not pole shoes with active structures for directing magnetic field as asserted.

claims.note: This reference does not mention a bevel on an active structure.
This reference does not mention a bevel or a bevel angle.
This reference does not mention a bevel angle or specific ranges for such an angle.

claims.quote: a plurality of pole sectors arranged within an envelope of the central bore and forming a workpiece contact interface of the magnetic device, each of the plurality of pole sectors comprising a plurality of spaced-apart pole portions arranged at respective
claims.note: The reference describes pole sectors with spaced-apart pole portions that form a workpiece contact interface, which can be interpreted as projections for directing the magnetic field and forming the contact surface.
claims.refuted: The quote describes pole portions separated by recesses, not projections forming workpiece contact surface as asserted.

claims.quote: each of the plurality of pole sectors comprising a plurality of spaced-apart pole portions arranged at respective distances, wherein a recess of a plurality of recesses separates each pole portion of the plurality of pole portions
claims.note: This passage describes a plurality of pole portions (projections) and recesses separating them, implying at least a first and second projection.
claims.refuted: The quote describes pole portions separated by recesses, not a first and second projection as asserted.

claims.quote: wherein a recess of a plurality of recesses separates each pole portion of the plurality of pole portions
claims.note: The quote indicates that pole portions are separated by recesses, which implies they are adjacent to one another.
claims.refuted: The quote describes recesses separating pole portions but does not establish that projections are adjacent to one another.

claims.quote: wherein a recess of a plurality of recesses separates each pole portion of the plurality of pole portions
claims.note: This passage explicitly states that a recess separates each pole portion, which means there is a recess between adjacent projections.

The reference discusses the depth and width of recesses in relation to the thickness of the ferromagnetic body, but it does not provide any teaching about the recess's depth or length deviating by at most 25% from the length of the projections.
The reference describes a magnetic device for coupling to a ferromagnetic body but does not disclose a specific positioning device for the workpiece.

claims.quote: wherein a first sector of the plurality of sectors form a first pole of the magnetic device and a second sector of the plurality of sectors form a second pole of the magnetic device
claims.note: The reference explicitly states that a first sector forms a first pole and a second sector forms a second pole, which corresponds to a first and second pole shoe.
claims.refuted: The quote describes sectors forming poles of the device, not pole shoes as asserted.

claims.quote: at least one first permanent magnet supported by the housing and having an active N-S pole pair; at least one second permanent magnet supported by the housing and having an active N-S pole pair
claims.note: The reference discloses N-S pole pairs for the permanent magnets and that a first sector forms a first pole and a second sector forms a second pole. However, it does not explicitly state that in a 'gripping position' the first pole shoe acts as a north pole and the second as a south pole, although this is implied by the N-S pole pairs and the formation of a magnetic circuit.

claims.quote: wherein the actuator is one of a hydraulic actuator, a pneumatic actuator, and an electrical actuator.
claims.note: The reference explicitly lists pneumatic and electrical actuators as options for moving the magnet, which aligns with the claim's 'electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically' displaceable magnet.
This reference does not mention a position sensor for detecting gripping or release positions.
This reference does not mention a workpiece sensor for detecting a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference does not mention a receptacle in the housing for a workpiece sensor or supply line.

claims.quote: The magnetic coupling device is carried by at least one selected from the group of: mechanical gantry, crane hoist, stationary fixture, and a robotic fixture.
claims.note: The reference discloses that the magnetic device can be carried by a robotic fixture, which implies an interface for attachment, but it does not explicitly mention a 'manipulator interface' or 'manipulator'.
This reference does not explicitly describe a housing portion designed to suppress the escape of the magnetic field.
This reference does not describe a specific shielding device to prevent magnetic field escape.

claims.quote: A magnetic device for magnetically coupling to a ferromagnetic body
claims.note: The reference describes a 'magnetic device for magnetically coupling to a ferromagnetic body', which is a magnetic gripper system, but does not explicitly use the term 'magnetic gripper system'.

claims.quote: A magnetic device for magnetically coupling to a ferromagnetic body
claims.note: The reference describes a 'magnetic device' which functions as a magnetic gripper, and it is designed for coupling to a 'ferromagnetic body', which is a ferromagnetic workpiece.

claims.quote: wherein the magnetic device establishes a first magnetic circuit with the at least one first permanent magnet and the at least one second permanent magnet through the plurality of pole sectors when the at least one second permanent magnet is
claims.note: This passage describes the establishment of a magnetic circuit when magnets are in a first position, which corresponds to a gripping state where a ferromagnetic body would be pressed by magnetic force.
claims.refuted: The quote describes establishing a magnetic circuit but does not mention pressing the workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.

claims.quote: and a second magnetic circuit with the first permanent magnet and the second permanent magnet when the second permanent magnet is positioned by the actuator in a second position relative to the at least one first permanent magnet.
claims.note: This passage describes a second magnetic circuit when the magnets are in a second position, which corresponds to a release state where the ferromagnetic workpiece is not pressed by magnetic force.
claims.refuted: The quote describes a second magnetic circuit in a second position but does not state the workpiece is not pressed against surfaces.

claims.quote: wherein at least one of the plurality of recesses has a depth substantially equal to a thickness of the ferromagnetic body to be coupled to the magnetic device.
claims.note: The reference teaches that the depth of recesses can be substantially equal to the thickness of the ferromagnetic body, which is related to the length of projections. However, it does not specify a deviation of at most 25%.
The reference does not mention a receptacle in the form of a groove.

overall.why: The reference describes a magnetic device with a housing, displaceable magnets, and pole sectors with structured contact surfaces, which aligns well with many core features of the subject invention, particularly the mechanism of operation and general structure.
